nodes.label: Action/AgentEvent loop pattern
nodes.rationale: smith-tui never talks to smith-providers or smith-tools directly, only through the Action/AgentEvent channels; this keeps the UI decoupled from orchestration so any new capability that must reach the UI needs a new AgentEvent variant, an emitter, and a handler arm rather than a direct call.

nodes.label: Tool interception pattern (ask_user)
nodes.rationale: ask_user is registered normally in ToolRegistry but its execute() is a stub that always errors; Agent::run_one_tool special-cases it by name before the generic dispatch and round-trips through a oneshot channel to the TUI instead. Use this pattern for any tool whose result depends on interactive UI state rather than trying to make ToolExecutor::execute itself interactive.

nodes.label: Permission model (PermissionClass/PermissionPolicy/plan_gated)
nodes.rationale: plan_gated blocks every tool above ReadOnly outright regardless of PermissionPolicy - even Skip doesn't bypass an unapproved plan - so plan approval is an independent, stronger gate layered on top of the per-tool permission classes.

nodes.label: Session/goal persistence
nodes.rationale: Session history and the goal are kept under the project's .smith/ directory (gitignored) rather than the global ~/.smith/config.toml, so project-scoped conversational state stays separate from global provider/model configuration.

nodes.label: Provider/model switching mid-session
nodes.rationale: messages: Vec<Message> lives independently of the Arc<dyn LlmProvider>, so conversation history carries over whether /model changes just the model or rebuilds the Agent against a different provider entirely.

nodes.label: Bug: Ollama 400 invalid message content type
nodes.rationale: OpenAI accepts content: null alongside tool_calls, but Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API requires content to be a string and rejects null. Fix: serialize empty assistant text as "" instead of JSON null (especially when tool_calls is present), and don't emit empty assistant wire messages with no tool_calls at all - this keeps the same serializer safe for both OpenAI and Ollama.

nodes.label: Language policy (English-only now, i18n later)
nodes.rationale: Ship everything in English as the default open-source standard for now rather than introducing a second locale; when adding strings, prefer centralizing them so i18n can be layered later without rewriting call sites.

nodes.label: Delivery principles (small independent packages)
nodes.rationale: Split work into small, independent packages, one command per coherent PR/commit, each usable in the TUI without depending on the next package, and avoid refactoring architecture beyond what the current package requires - keeps incremental delivery reviewable.

nodes.label: Acceptance criteria (per package)
nodes.rationale: Each package must register the slash command with documented args, behave predictably with friendly errors, persist state where continuity is needed, avoid regressing streaming/cancel/permission/clear, and add unit tests for pure logic - the bar for calling any package 'done'.
